 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 31.12.2023 at about 2.00 a.m, after finishing of new year celebration the deceased and other friends were going from Bengaluru to Mysore and they were proceeding in a Kia car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MT-3764, the same was driven by one Kapisha Vimal on Bengaluru - Mysore Express way, on the way SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 at about 3.00 a.m, (early morning) when they reached near Garudana Ukkada Express Way, Garudana Ukkada Village, Srirangapatna Taluk, Mandya District, at that all of a sudden the driver of Fiat car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-Z-2540 without giving any indication and putting lights coming from opposite direction from service road and enter into Express highway in a rash and negligent manner due to the terrific impact the driver of the Kia car lost control over the said vehicle and dashed to the rear side of the Fiat car.
Due to the said impact the car moved ahead and dashed to concrete divider and caused the accident.
Consequent to which the deceased and the inmates of the car sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further urged that immediately after the accident deceased and others persons were shifted to Srirangapatna Government Hospital, wherein the duty doctors examined and declared him dead on the way to the hospital.

Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies and they have spent substantial amount towards medical expenses, SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Fiat car and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
5. After service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement and contending that the petitions itself are not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-Z-2540.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Non -compliance of sections 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.

This respondent specifically and SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the Rajeev Kumar Singh vs Vinay Prasad K R on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145323759/
2 vehicle in the accident.

sentences.text: Negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is contended that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MT-3764 in which the deceased was proceeding.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid &
effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 01.01.2024 at about 3.00 a.m, (early morning) near Garudana Ukkada Express Way, Garudana Ukkada Village, Srirangapatna Taluk, Mandya District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Fiat Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-Z-2540 ?

3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
7. Petitioner No.2 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 19 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
In order to prove the defence, The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
8. Heard counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  SCCH-23  MVC.No.4459/2024 Rajeev Kumar Singh vs Vinay Prasad K R on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145323759/
3  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.2 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.35 lakhs together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of Fiat car for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337,
304(A) of IPC and u/s 184 of MV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Fiat SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 car.

With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE No.1 :
The petitioners claim that Petitioner No.1 & 2 are the parents of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.2 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhaar cards and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondent.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE No.3:
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.35 lakhs due to the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.

It is the specific defence urged by the petitioners counsel that the deceased was aged 20 years SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 and pursuing his BE 5th Semester at Manipal College, Udupi and also doing part time job and thereby earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m and as such, he had a bright future and because of his ill-fated accident which has become the bolt from the blue for the family of the petitioners.
It is also vociferously urged that in twinkling of eye whole family structure of the family of the petitioners is demolished by this ill-fated accident.
13. In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this Court.

Further the learned counsel for respondent No.2 filed written arguments stated that the petitioners have not produced any piece of documents with regard to deceased was studying 5th Semester B.E. and also doing part time job and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m, but not produced any documents in this regard, even they have not produced Marks cards or certificates to show that he was studying BE.
Hence, in the absence of income proof, only notional income to be taken into consideration.

It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

14. The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P13 wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 03.03.2004, which SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 indicates that he was aged (19 years 9 months 29 days) 20 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '18'.
15.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 20 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased was aged about 20 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e., 40%).
SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 16.
Further as stated above that deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation

, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards her personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for her personal expenditure.

On such deduction,
the income of the deceased comes to Rs.11,200/- p.m. (Rs.22,400/- X 50/100).
17. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,200/- p.m. and the multiplier "18" is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.24,19,200/- (Rs.11,200 X 12 X 18)

Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.24,19,200/- under the head of loss of Rajeev Kumar Singh vs Vinay Prasad K R on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145323759/
5 dependency.

sentences.text: 18. In this case, petitioner No.1 & 2 are the father and mother of the deceased and

as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a daughter causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their daughter during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

19. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

20. The calculation table stands as follows :
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.
Towards loss of dependency Rs.24,19,200-00 SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 2. Towards loss of Filial Consortium Rs. 80,000-00 to the petitioners
Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150-00 4.
Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150-00 body funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses Total Rs.25,35,500-00 21.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of car thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024

sentences.text: ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,35,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 50%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 & 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer & printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 5th day of December - 2025).
(Shreyansh Doddamani) XXI Addl. Small Causes Judge & ACJM, Bengaluru.

Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of car thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,35,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 50%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 & 2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to them through E-payment SCCH-23 MVC.No.4459/2024 on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 & 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
